parsed_profile_json.title: 7FA TURBINE SHELL INLET BLEED HEAT (IBH) EXTRACTION PIPE WELD CRACKING
parsed_profile_json.reason_for_revision: The purpose of revision is to provide recommended inspection intervals and update the affected unit list and application to include 7F, 7FA and 7FA+.
parsed_profile_json.purpose: To recommend inspection of 7FA turbine shell IBH extraction port cover flange pipes for potential weld cracking, and to specify corrective action if required.
parsed_profile_json.compliance_category_text: Safety - Failure to comply with this TIL could result in personal injury. Compliance is mandated within a specific operating time.
scope_of_work: Dye penetrant inspection of the weld joint on 7FA turbine shell IBH extraction port cover flange pipes by a certified level II NDT inspector.

If cracks are found, perform repair (grind off cracked section and repair weld per GE weld specification P8A-AG3 or equivalent) or replacement (replace flange and install new flange gasket per MLI-0705 assembly drawing), then re-inspect per the recommended schedule.
service_recommendation_line_items: Perform dye penetrant inspection of the pipe to cover flange weld joint by a certified level II NDT inspector: first inspection at the first Hot Gas Path inspection (HGPI); if beyond first HGPI, inspect at the next planned shutdown opportunity.
Re-inspect the IBH weld joint at every HGPI/Major inspection, or at a convenient planned outage.

If cracks are indicated on the pipe or on the weld: Option 1 Repair—grind off cracked section and perform repair welding using GE weld specification P8A-AG3 or equivalent; Option 2 Replacement—replace the flange with a new part and replace the flange gasket; install per MLI-0705 assembly drawing.
Re-inspect repaired, replaced, and original IBH weld joint per the schedule (first HGPI / next planned shutdown if beyond first HGPI; then every HGPI/Major or convenient planned outage).

source_snippets.snippet: To recommend inspection of 7FA turbine shell IBH extraction port cover flange pipes for potential weld cracking, and to specify corrective action if required.

GE recommends dye penetrant inspection of the weld joint by a certified level II NDT inspector at the following intervals: a. First inspection at the first Hot Gas Path inspection (HGPI). If beyond first HGPI, then at the next planned shutdown opportunity. b. Re-inspection at every HGPI/Major inspection, or at a convenient planned outage.

If inspections indicate cracks on the pipe or on the weld, corrective action is recommended per the following options: Option 1: Repair • Grind off the cracked section of the structure. Use GE weld specification P8A-AG3 or equivalent to perform repair welding. Option 2: Replacement • Replace the flange with a new part. A new flange gasket will also be required. Install per the MLI-0705 assembly drawing.

The crack initiated at the pipe to cover flange weld as shown in Figure 2, and resulted in substantial hot air leakage. This type of leakage can cause elevated turbine compartment temperatures that could lead to a forced outage condition, and are also a safety concern.
